title: Priv EKS terraform lifecycle module with health webhooks and canary adapters
creator: Alyssa Cheng
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that provisions and manages the Redwood Private control plane (EKS) components in customer VPCs. The module must provide an idempotent lifecycle API for bootstrapping control plane resources, an opinionated upgrade strategy with staged rollouts/canaries, and pluggable health-check webhook hooks that integrate with our observability and rollback tooling. This ticket focuses on the module interface, preflight/health webhooks, and wiring for canary rollouts; subsequent tickets will cover provider-specific installers and docs.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes a minimal, well-documented input set to provision control-plane resources (IAM roles, control-plane security groups, ECR access, control-plane launch templates).
Module supports a 'canary' flag and staging parameters to apply upgrades to a configurable subset of nodes/control-plane endpoints before global rollout.
Health-check webhooks are emitted during create/update/destroy lifecycle events and are received by the Redwood Console observability endpoint (test receiver) for validation.
Module runs idempotently across repeated applies and includes preflight validations for networking, KMS keys, and service quotas; failure modes are documented and fail-fast with meaningful messages.
Automated integration test harness exists (terraform apply/destroy in ephemeral account) and a sample PR demonstrates a canary upgrade and automated rollback on health-check failure.
implementation_notes: Design the module as two layers: 'controlplane_core' (immutable resources) and 'controlplane_lifecycle' (upgrade & canary orchestration).
Expose an outputs map containing cluster endpoint, control-plane role ARNs, health webhook signing key, and canary target identifiers.
Health webhooks: publish JSON payloads to an SNS topic with HMAC signature header; Redwood observability will subscribe and validate signatures. Provide a local 'test-receiver' option for CI.

Upgrade strategy: support 'percent' and 'count' canary selection rules, with a configurable wait window and health probe retries. Provide terraform null_resource hooks to trigger canary orchestration state machine (Step Function) rather than blocking the apply for long windows.
Preflight checks: verify VPC CIDR allocations, route table connectivity to control-plane subnets, EKS quota estimates, and KMS key access. Fail before creating resources if checks do not pass.
Testing: add a 'smoke' variant in our CI that applies the module to a shared dev account using small instance types and then runs control-plane readiness probes + webhook validation.
Backward compatibility: keep existing modules intact; provide a gradual migration plan and a compatibility layer to translate old variables to the new input shape.
Security: generate webhook signing keys in KMS; mark security_review_required = true and schedule a design review with Security team.
